findings.finding: Yoga-fire body abandonment, own-māyā reappearance as Himācala’s daughter, Śiva meditation, severe tapas and renewed husband relationship are explicit. Daughter relation and rebirth must retain their distinct source contexts.

The source explicitly gives three heads, three feet and trident, arising from Śiva’s struck matted hair while Gaṇeśa is remembered. Servant declaration, command against Dakṣa with sacrifice, world-shaking laugh, body-generated Rudras and following Gaṇas are supported; this is manifestation rather than ordinary biological birth.

The named duel assignments and actions match the Sanskrit. Bhairava makes Indra unconscious; Śiva, rather than Vīrabhadra, breaks Pūṣan’s teeth and removes Bhaga’s eyes. Nandin seizes Dharma, Bhṛṅgin Kaśyapa, Puṣpadanta strikes Varuṇa, Vīrabhadra fells Dakṣa, and Śiva fells Viṣṇu with heart-directed arrows after Gaṇeśa contemplation.

Nārāyaṇa and Pāśupata missiles fight in the sky; their fire and frightened worlds, Dakṣa’s head offered into fire by Vīrabhadra, and cakra bowing and stopping before Śiva are supported. The beast comparison is locally ritual framing, not a goat-head precondition.

Heavenly voice remains unidentified. Viṣṇu survives the intended trident attack; Brahmā pacifies Śiva, assigns remaining offerings and requests restoration. Bhaga gets eyes, Pūṣan becomes a ground-food eater, and other attendees regain their former forms/radiance.

The burnt head causes the first-seen-being head instruction. Bhṛṅgin kills the seen goat, Śiva attaches the head and revives Dakṣa, and Brahmā prompts the hymn. Goat-head revival is an intermediate event.

The pardon request, goat-like voiced praise, subsequent human-head restoration, announced Prajāpati chiefship and separate hymn/sound benefits are explicit. The witness does not leave Dakṣa permanently goat-headed. Once qualifies the goat-like sound before Śiva; no numerical repetition restriction is given for the hymn here.

All five emanation sites are supported: navel, mouth, eye, left side and right side. Śiva explicitly addresses Pārvatī as Śakti in this cosmic narrative. COSMOLOGICAL_EMANATION and the local speech qualifier correctly preserve this without replacing the Himācala daughter/rebirth account.

Brahmā’s haṃsa, Viṣṇu’s Garuḍa and Hara’s bull, together with their named stations/functions and four-face/four-arm/five-face qualifications, are supported. Third-eye burning is explicitly assigned to Hara.

Sūrya’s horse-adorned chariot and Śakti’s lion match this text; no horse number is supplied. Thousand rays, six seasons, rain source, Sauraloka and Śaktiloka are explicit. Weapons, ornaments, varied powers and fulfilled resolve are a collective final grant.

findings.finding: Viṣṇu first requests a boon from Brahmā, Brahmā offers it, Viṣṇu specifies Brahmā as his son, and Brahmā accepts because of his own offered promise. Brahmā explicitly promises yoga-created body from Viṣṇu’s navel-lotus at creation. Grantor Brahmā / recipient Viṣṇu is securely established here; no ordinary biological birth is implied.

Viṣṇu urges Brahmā’s request so Śiva will be his own grandson through Brahmā. Brahmā asks Śiva to become his son, Viṣṇu repeats, and Śiva promises a future partial Rudra manifestation from Brahmā’s forehead. The patch correctly treats this as future local manifestation/genealogy, not immediate ordinary biological birth.

Śiva retrospectively narrates the five-deity rivalry, following Gaṇeśa instruction/disappearance, great tapas to obtain her and her satisfaction after one hundred years. Śakti appears and invites a boon, Śiva bows/praises and asks her wifehood; she grants and disappears. Hundred years belongs to the austerity circumstances, not a marriage-expiry restriction or grant duration. Patch agency and field placement are supported.
Lakṣmī emerges from her left limb, Sāvitrī from right, Saṃjñā from heart. EMANATION labels preserve the locally stated origins without forcing a human birth mechanism.

The wording is Nārāyaṇa-priyā for Lakṣmī, Brahmā-priyā for Sāvitrī, and explicit wife of Ravi for Saṃjñā. The patch correctly preserves beloved_of versus spouse_of here rather than silently treating all three as identical marriage statements.

Pārvatī follows renewed Gaṇeśa yoga privately, gains peace in a short time through prior impressions and goes to Śiva’s vicinity. No fixed number of years for her practice is supplied; the patch does not transfer Śiva’s hundred years to her.
